Shameless Snacks · Meta · creative diagnosis

What the ads say vs what the customers say

600 creatives (92% of $1,956,132 90-day Meta spend, 2026-07-28 to 2026-10-26) tagged by persona, angle, awareness stage, format and on-camera talent, diffed against 10,168 top-level Facebook ad comments (2026-04-26 to 2026-10-26) tagged the same way. Same classifier both sides. Method: Dara Denney's ads-vs-reviews diff; comments are the review corpus.

$1,956,132spend, all 4,379 creatives
0.81ROAS (platform-attributed)
0.52CM-ROAS (rev − COGS) / spend
-$934,482contribution (rev − COGS − spend)
-59%CM % of revenue, first-order
10,168comments · 5,342 customer voice

Source: ejam-dwh production.creative_dashboard (brand SHA, channel facebook) + ai.asset_tagging_video/static + production.facebook_dashboard_comments. Contribution here is before agency and merchant fees. Negative first-order CM is normal for SHA; subscriptions pay back on rebills. Comment share is not buyer share: doubters and flavor opinions over-comment. Sizing comes from the Sep-2026 survey; this page is about who is talking and what they say vs who the ads are cast and written for.

0. The diagnosis

The account is telling a young man's calorie-and-offer story to a 45-to-65-year-old woman who buys for taste, stays for fiber, and will not try it until someone she trusts tells her on camera that it will not wreck her stomach.
1 · Cast the buyerBrief a 40-plus female personal-history pack across CandySnob, GutFixer and BloodSugarManager. Female 30-54 talent carries 6% of spend today; female 55+ carries $0.
2 · Answer the SkepticOne educational-breakdown ad on what is in it and how to eat it the first week (allulose and erythritol, half a bag). The #1 objection and the #1 complaint are the same sentence. Compliance: helps-verbs only, no laxative or medical claims.
3 · Taste as the lead, not the proof pointTaste is 33% of customer voice and 5% of spend. Move a quarter of Product-aware LowCal/Offer budget into Problem-aware taste-first and stomach-safe entries.
Mechanisms named on this pageThe stat duelPermission by abundanceSarah's orderShelf proofThe unanswered 'what's in it'Cast is not buyerTaste is the entry, fiber is the stay

PermissionSeeker + CalorieCounter are the account's story. 37% of spend, 7% of voice. They convert (CM -41% / -64%), so this is not "stop". It is "they are the only story being told".
The customer's own words are taste and regularity. CandySnob + GutFixer + Fibermaxxer = 33% of voice, 18% of spend. The survey agrees: taste is why 62 to 68% came back.
The Skeptic is the prospect. 27% of all comments, 1.3% of spend. Section 4 has what they doubt.
BloodSugarManager is under-funded against the survey, not the comments. 34% of buyers manage blood sugar (Norwest); ads give the persona 0.5%. Diabetics do not announce it on a candy ad, so the survey wins this one.
Parents and SugarQuitter are over-funded against voice. 5.4% / 4.4% of spend, under 1% of voice each. Parents was already retired as a priority ICP.

7. The top 24 spenders, one by one

55% of 90-day spend. Each gets what worked and what held it back. Account baseline: ROAS 0.81, CM -59%. Codes open the asset; "post" opens the Facebook post with its comments.

▶
▶ SH-16975-3 CalorieCounter · LowCal · Solution-aware · transformation comparison · talent male under30
$202,525 spend-$107,986 contribution-73% CM0.73 ROAS2,293 orderspost ↗
This one bag is 880 calories.
What workedThe stat duel. One bag vs one bag and a number nobody expected (880 calories). The hook is a mechanic, not a line, which is why it carried a third of September and 2,293 orders.
What held it backCast and written for a 24-year-old man doing calorie math; the buyer is a woman over 45. Worst contribution of the top five, fatigued by its own week 2, and it never says what is in the bag, so it feeds the Skeptic without answering him.
▶
▶ SH-16975-2 PermissionSeeker · Offer · Product-aware · product demo · talent male under30
$127,872 spend-$39,613 contribution-29% CM1.06 ROAS1,601 orderspost ↗
Yes, you get this entire box of shameless snacks on a huge discount today
What workedOffer-first with the whole box on the counter. 'Yes, you get this entire box' tells a Product-aware buyer exactly what lands at her door; best contribution of the big spenders.
What held it backPure offer. It only works on someone who already believes the product. Nothing for the 27% of commenters who doubt it, and the hands and voice are a young man's.
▣
▣ SH-17273-9 NightSnacker · Cravings · Problem-aware · authority · talent none none
$100,770 spend-$60,067 contribution-94% CM0.63 ROAS1,022 orderspost ↗
Amazon's Record-Breaking Candy feeds cravings. 26g of fiber. flips candy logic on its head.
What workedA static that works as a cold entry is rare: Problem-aware (cravings) plus social-proof volume ('Amazon's record-breaking candy') scaled past $100k.
What held it backThird-worst contribution margin in the top ten. 'Record-breaking' proves popularity, not safety, and three claims are stacked in one headline. Its clone SH-17273-4 at 0.64 shows the format is tapped.
▶
▶ SH-16180-1 NightSnacker · Offer · Product-aware · product demo · talent male under30
$94,239 spend-$38,632 contribution-45% CM0.91 ROAS1,257 orderspost ↗
not one, not two, not three, not four, but 12 bags of shameless snacks
What workedCounting haul: 'not one, not two... 12 bags'. Quantity reveal makes abundance the hook and restock framing implies a habit.
What held it backThe fourth count-up haul in the top twenty with the same mechanic (the two Cruva copies run 0.83 and 0.70). The mechanic is spent, and the buyer is watching a young man's pantry.
▣
▣ SH-13376-6 Parents · LowCal · Product-aware · authority · talent none none
$73,263 spend-$24,243 contribution-32% CM1.03 ROAS922 orderspost ↗
SPOTTED AT TARGET:
What workedShelf proof. 'Spotted at Target' makes the brand real and lowers first-try risk; 1.03 on a static.
What held it backIt says 'we exist', not 'here is why'. Parents persona gets 5.4% of spend for 0.8% of voice, and the sibling 'NOW AT TARGET' at 0.97 shows the lift is the logo. Also points buyers at Target, not the site.
▣
▣ SH-13376-9 Unknown · None · Product-aware · authority · talent none none
$44,816 spend-$16,646 contribution-38% CM0.97 ROAS530 orderspost ↗
NOW AT TARGET.
What workedSame shelf proof, cheaper to make, near account ROAS.
What held it backA duplicate of SH-13376-6 with less context. No persona, no angle; the account keeps buying the Target logo instead of a message.
▣
▣ SHA_CC_WK22_Im GutFixer · GutHealth · Problem-aware · authority · talent none none
$43,374 spend-$17,441 contribution-44% CM0.92 ROAS509 orderspost ↗
At Last! A Candy That's Good For Your Gut Health
What workedThe only top-ten ad that leads with the customer's second reason to stay (gut and fiber). Advertorial 'At last!' headline is a Problem-aware entry with near-average contribution on cold traffic.
What held it back'Good for your gut health' is a claim with no mechanism and no number. It is the one ad where a doubter would look for 'what happens to my stomach', and it does not say.
▣
▣ SHA_CC_WK22_He Unknown · None · Unaware · other · talent none none
$41,373 spend-$20,547 contribution-63% CM0.79 ROAS477 orderspost ↗
visual-only open
What workedProduct-only hero: clean, no claim risk, pure recognition at scale.
What held it backSays nothing. No persona, no angle, no entry stage. $41k on a billboard with no argument, and the second-worst contribution in the top ten.
▣
▣ SH-14498-8 PermissionSeeker · Offer · Product-aware · offer promo · talent none none
$33,992 spend-$14,446 contribution-48% CM0.88 ROAS378 orderspost ↗
HOLY SH*T ALL OF THIS FOR FREE!
What workedBrand voice ('HOLY SH*T') plus the whole gift stack framed as 'all of this'. Offer clarity in four words.
What held it back'FREE' on a $30-plus cart pulls deal-seekers; subscription is 10% of complaints. Offer-only, Product-aware, no reason to believe for a first-timer.

▶ SH-12937-7 CandySnob · Taste · Product-aware · educational breakdown · talent female under30
$32,561 spend-$9,694 contribution-28% CM1.08 ROAS439 orderspost ↗
Three claims about Shameless Snacks.
What workedThe only educational-breakdown ad in the top 24 and it is above 1.0. 'Three claims, true or false' lets the doubter test the brand; packing-floor setting is proof of a real operation; female talent.
What held it backUnder-30 talent, and the claims are macros, not 'what is in it and what it does to your stomach'. Third ad in the account built on the warehouse-packing bit.

▶ Cruva · @yaboy NightSnacker · DailyHabit · Product-aware · personal story · talent male under30
$22,790 spend-$10,923 contribution-59% CM0.81 ROAS247 orderspost ↗
So there's a reason why I get bags and bags of this candy.
What workedPersonal-habit story ('there's a reason I buy bags and bags') is the personal-history format Denney asks for, with haul proof on screen.
What held it backA young man telling a routine story to a 50-year-old woman. 'Bags and bags' is volume, not a reason. Contribution -59%.

▶ SH-15191-5 GutFixer · GutHealth · Product-aware · product demo · talent male under30
$21,198 spend-$6,106 contribution-26% CM1.10 ROAS284 orderspost ↗
All right, Sarah, love your choices.
What workedSarah's order. A real customer's name and picks on screen is social proof plus personalisation; replying to a comment is literally comments-as-ads. 1.10 ROAS and the best contribution in the top 15.
What held it backProduct-aware only: you have to know the brand to care about Sarah's order. The format is now four deep (SH-16212-3, -10 siblings) and gut health is incidental to the packing bit.

visual-only open

don't get these, don't get these, definitely don't get these cuz right now you can get them in a variety pack, try all the flavors in one shot on a me

8. Mechanisms

The stat duel

A comparison hook is a mechanic, not a line. One bag vs one bag with a number nobody expected. Carried a third of September; copies decay fast (SH-16975-3, JeremyMorrison, SamuelMatz).

Permission by abundance

Hauls, unboxings and count-ups sell 'you get a lot' to a buyer who already wants it. 19% of spend, under 1% of customer voice; works on Product-aware traffic only.

Sarah's order

Replying to a real comment on camera (order-packing with the customer's name) is proof plus personalisation. Best contribution of any format in the top 15; now four ads deep.

Shelf proof

'Spotted at Target' says the brand is real. It lowers risk without giving a reason, and the lift is the logo: each copy earns less.

The unanswered 'what's in it'

Sugar alcohols and stomach are the #1 objection (26%) and the #1 complaint (18%). 3.5% of spend touches it, mostly by attacking competitor bars. Customers answer it for each other in the comments ('half a bag, twice a day').

Cast is not buyer

Under-30 talent carries 44% of spend, male 37%. Buyer is a woman 45 to 65. Female 30-54 talent: 6% of spend. Female 55+: $0.

Taste is the entry, fiber is the stay

Taste is 33% of customer voice and 5% of spend; the survey says taste is why 62-68% came back. The account leads with calories and offers, which is the account's story, not hers.

Method and definitions

  • Ads. creative_dashboard, brand SHA, channel facebook, 2026-07-28 to 2026-10-26; per-creative spend, revenue, COGS, orders plus BQ AI tags (awareness_level, talent archetype and demographics, pain_named, promise_type). Top 600 by spend classified by Gemini 2.5 Flash (temperature 0.1, no thinking) into persona (canon archetypes + 5 segment tokens), angle (canon), awareness, format bucket, talent age and gender.
  • Comments. facebook_dashboard_comments, top-level comments of 25+ characters, 2026-04-26 to 2026-10-26, 10,168 unique. Same classifier adds comment type, customer flag, quote-worthy flag. Customer voice = 5,342 comments that are testimonials, praise, complaints or flavor feedback, or where the writer says they bought.
  • Contribution = revenue − COGS − spend, platform-attributed, first-order, before agency and merchant fees. CM % = contribution / revenue. CM-ROAS = (revenue − COGS) / spend. Negative first-order CM is normal for SHA; subscriptions pay back on rebills.
  • Themes in section 4 are keyword groups applied inside the LLM type labels; a comment can match more than one theme.
  • Single-pass labels are directional. Same classifier on both sides, so the diffs are internally valid; do not compare with the Aug-2026 keyword ranking. Re-run quarterly with prep.py → build_preview.py in projects/2026-10/sha-ads-vs-comments-diff.
  • Wiki page: Shameless Snacks / customer / voice-of-customer / ads-vs-comments-diff-2026-10. Method page: Creative Strategy / testing-and-analysis / creative-diagnosis-and-creator-formats-2026.
